subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to Telegram blocked-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should this issue define a broader MEDIA root policy?
rationale: The source-reproducible failure is clear, but broadening allowed host-local `MEDIA:` paths changes a filesystem read/upload boundary and overlaps an existing open root-policy item.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots in existing policy item
options.body: Keep this issue for clearer Telegram/media failure feedback and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved filesystem-roots design own persistent root expansion.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical place to specify, implement, document, and prove a supported configurable MEDIA root contract.

options.title: Close as designed after docs check
options.body: Treat out-of-root MEDIA directives as intentional safe-default behavior and require users to move files under managed roots or use the message tool path.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots in existing policy item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue for clearer Telegram/media failure feedback and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved filesystem-roots design own persistent root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the current outbound media access policy and the July 2026 media-root implementation lines.
